title: Paraoxonase 1 and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Meta-Analysis Protocol
author: Jun Watanabe
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bza3p2gn

steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Search MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL electronic databases using specific keywords and MeSH terms to identify studies on PON1 activity in COPD.

substeps.instruction: Apply search terms for PON1: 'PON1', 'paraoxonase', 'arylesterase', and 'aryldialkylphosphatase'.
Apply search terms for COPD: 'chronic obstructive pulmonary disease', 'emphysema', 'chronic bronchitis', 'COPD', 'COAD', 'COBD', and 'AECB'.
Search the reference lists of all eligible studies identified.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Independently screen retrieved articles to determine eligibility based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate full texts of potentially relevant summaries independently.
Include clinical studies focusing on PON1 activity in patients with stable COPD compared to healthy controls.
Exclude studies without healthy controls or those focusing on PON1 in asthma patients.
Confirm eligibility only when two researchers are in agreement.

steps.title: Evaluate Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Assess the quality of the included non-randomized studies using the Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Rating Scale (NOS).

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.instruction: Create a summary table for each eligible article to extract relevant data.

steps.title: Perform Meta-Analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct meta-analyses using random-effects models in Review Manager 5.4.1 (RevMan 2020).

substeps.instruction: Calculate the standard mean difference (SMD) and 95% confidence interval (CI) of paraoxonase and arylesterase activity.
Calculate missing standard deviations using Cochrane handbook methods, Altman's method (if only standard error or p-value is reported), or validated methods using confidence interval and t-value.

steps.title: Evaluate Heterogeneity
steps.instruction: Assess statistical heterogeneity using visual inspection of forest plots and the I2 statistic.

substeps.instruction: Interpret I2 values: 0-40% (might not be important), 30-60% (moderate), 50-90% (substantial), 75-100% (considerable).
If heterogeneity is identified (I2 > 50%), perform subgroup analyses based on COPD severity.
Judge severity based on the prevalence of severe COPD patients or the use of home oxygen therapy.

description: 2 Abstract Introduction: Oxidative stress is a driving factor in the pathophysiology of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). While paraoxonase 1 (PON1) is an antioxidant enzyme, a potential biomarker of this disease, data regarding the relationship of PON-1 with COPD appear to show some controversy. In this regard, to shed light on this issue, we will aim to perform a meta-analysis of data on PON1 activity in COPD. Methods: Electronic databases (MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL) will be searched for available studies on PON1 activity in patients with stable COPD published before October 2021. A meta-analysis will be performed using random-effects models. Key words: antioxidant; arylesterase; chronic obstructive lung disease; reactive oxygen species; paraoxonase 3 Introduction Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), a progressive airway disorder, is a major cause of death and disability worldwide, and the number of patients is increasing [1]. Smoking, air pollution and increased free radicals in the respiratory tract cause an increased burden of oxidative stress, leading to the development and progression of COPD [2,3]. Oxidative stress is reported to induce structural changes in the essential components of the lung, including irreversible damage to both the parenchyma and airway wall [4]. In this process, various molecules, such as nucleic acids, lipids and proteins, are oxidized [5]. Currently, oxidative stress is considered a crucial contributor to the pathophysiology of COPD [6–8]. The burden of oxidative stress is modified by the antioxidant balance. Paraoxonase 1 (PON1), which is known as an antioxidant enzyme, is composed of 354 amino acids with a molecular weight 43 kDa and is encoded by the PON1 gene [9]. PON1 activity is determined by the substrates used to measure it, in particular, arylesterase (when using phenylacetate) and paraoxonase (when using paraoxon).
